property_summary: For any payable amount and any external callee address that REVERTS on receiving funds, the reference C forwards the call to that callee and always ends with the contract balance being zero (owner always successfully receives remaining balance via transfer), while the mutant that uses call to send the remaining balance can fail to transfer to owner when the callee reverts or causes gas/forwarding differences, leaving address(c).balance > 0 for some inputs.

For any caller and any ether amount sent to go(), contract C always ends with balance == 0 (it forwards funds to a fixed target and then guarantees the owner receives the remaining balance via transfer); the mutant that replaces the final transfer with call can leave address(c).balance > 0 for some adversarial callee behavior, so the invariant balance == 0 is violated.

For any caller and any sent value, after go() completes the contract's balance is always zero (reference uses transfer to ensure owner receives remaining balance); the mutant that uses call to pay the owner can fail to forward funds for some adversarial callee behavior, leaving address(c).balance > 0.

For any caller and any payable amount, after go() completes the reference contract always has zero balance (it reliably transfers remaining balance to owner via transfer); the mutant that uses call to pay the owner can leave address(c).balance > 0 when the external target causes a reversion or malicious behavior, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any sent value, after go() completes the reference contract C always has zero balance (it guarantees owner is paid via transfer), whereas the mutant that replaces transfer with call can fail to forward the remaining balance to owner for some adversarial callee behavior, leaving address(c).balance > 0.
